items.title: CBH's FY26 orderbook target raised to RM800mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) has raised CBH Engineering Holding Bhd's financial year 2026 (FY26) orderbook replenishment assumption to RM800 million from RM600 million, supported by its stronger-than-expected data centre (DC) pipeline. The company's year-to-date replenishment stands at RM482.7 million, following the latest win of an RM88.1 million contract. CBH Engineering Sdn Bhd, CBH's wholly-owned subsidiary, secured the RM88.1 million design-and-build contract for a 275kV consumer landing station serving a DC in Selangor.

items.title: Two Kota Kinabalu bus workers come to blows over passengers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A dispute over securing passengers is believed to have led to a fight between two bus company workers at the Inanam Bus Terminal in Kota Kinabalu last Friday. Kota Kinabalu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said police received a report on the incident on the same day. Earlier, a 29-second video showing the two men fighting at the Inanam Bus Terminal went viral on social media.

items.title: Pedestrian killed in hit-and-run on LDP, Proton Saga driver flees
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — A local man in his 40s was killed after being hit by a Proton Saga in a hit-and-run incident at Kilometer 0.8 of the Damansara-Puchong Expressway (LDP) towards Puchong early yesterday morning. Petaling Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police received information about the incident at about 5.40am, according to Kosmo! Members of the public can also contact the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters operations room at 03-79662222.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines flight to Jeddah diverted to Chennai over suspected engine problem
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A Malaysia Airlines flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jeddah was diverted to Chennai, India on Monday after a suspected problem with one of its engines, according to Indian media reports. According to national news agency Bernama, citing a report by the Times of India , flight MH156, carrying 186 passengers, made an emergency landing at Chennai Airport before the aircraft was moved to a parking bay, while passengers were provided accommodation at the airport. The Hindu, citing Airports Authority of India (AAI) officials, reported that the flight departed Kuala Lumpur at 3.30pm before the pilot suspected an engine malfunction and requested permission to land in Chennai.

items.title: Firefighter swims 50m to rescue man who jumped from Kuala Selangor bridge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Quick action by firefighters saved a man who jumped from the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah 5 Bridge in Kuala Selangor last night. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Division assistant director Asrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 8.05pm, with five firefighters from the Kuala Selangor Fire and Rescue Station involved in the operation. He said the firefighters, who arrived five minutes later, immediately began the rescue operation.

items.title: #NSTviral: Anwar notices graduate's speech inspired by his own, jokes about 'royalties'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A young graduate who drew inspiration from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's speech for his own graduation address has caught the attention of the man himself. I learned from Datuk Seri's speech," he wrote. Awwal replied: "Thank you, Datuk Seri!

items.title: Pas-Umno unity possible if parties willing to compromise on seats, says Pas spiritual leader
items.summary: ARAU: Political cooperation between Pas and Umno can be achieved if the two largest Malay-based parties compromise on seat allocations ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16). Pas spiritual leader Datuk Hashim Jasin said reviving ties between the two parties is nothing new as they have cooperated before, adding that Malay voters want to see the partnership continue. The current political climate clearly requires Pas and Umno to work together."

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: Transport problems threatening school attendance of 989 Labuan students, 437 to get aid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A total of 989 students from 25 schools in the Federal Territory of Labuan have been identified as facing school attendance issues, with transportation among the main contributing factors. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, in a post on Facebook, said that, as a start, 437 students across six schools would receive assistance through the Student School Transportation Facility in the Federal Territory of Labuan. She said the initiative was being implemented through collaboration between the Federal Territories Department and Labuan Corporation, the Labuan Federal Territory Education Department, schools, Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) and the industry, particularly the Labuan Mini Bus Operators Association.

items.title: Fire at FRIM Bidor burns 2.42ha forest area, operation resumes this morning
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 8 — About 2.42 hectares of forest area at the Forest Research Institute of Malaysia (FRIM) in Bidor caught fire in an incident yesterday evening. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said his department received a call about the fire at 5.42 pm before a team of personnel from the Bidor Fire and Rescue Station was rushed to the location. “The operation continued last night with a change of personnel at the location.

items.title: Anwar congratulates Tunku Mahkota Ismail after Royal Johor triumphs, Regent named MVP of Johor Super Crown Polo tournament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his congratulations to Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Regent of Johor, on being named the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament (JSCPT) 2026. “Congratulations to His Royal Highness Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Regent of Johor, on being named the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament 2026, while also leading Royal Johor to lift this prestigious title,” he said. Tunku Mahkota Ismail was named the MVP of JSCPT 2026 yesterday after delivering an outstanding performance throughout the prestigious tournament.

items.title: Thailand’s Sihasak departs Malaysia after two-day visit focused on border security, development and smuggling
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 8 — Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sihasak Phuangketkeow departed for home after concluding his two-day working visit to Malaysia. In 2025, Thailand was the sixth largest trading partner globally and the second largest among Asean Member States, with total trade amounting to RM118.57 billion (US$27.73 billion). From January to July 2026, bilateral trade between the two countries reached RM85.01 billion (US$21.13 billion), compared with RM66.95 billion (US$16.64 billion) during the corresponding period in 2025, reflecting the continued strong growth and potential of economic ties between the two countries.

items.title: Two men with 65 criminal records between them arrested over 12 house-breaking cases
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Sept 8 — Police arrested two men in a raid in Teluk Kemang on Sept 3 to assist in investigations into 12 house-breaking cases in Negeri Sembilan, Perak and Kedah. Port Dickson police chief Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan said both suspects, aged 24 and 34, were picked up around 4 pm by the district Criminal Investigation Division. He said background checks revealed that the first suspect has 54 prior criminal records and is wanted in two outstanding cases, while the second suspect has 11 prior criminal records.

items.title: Maritime industry expert urges clearer timelines for probes, says prolonged uncertainty hurts businesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Maritime industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan has called for clear timelines to be set for investigations into alleged corruption and other misconduct, saying prolonged probes without clear updates could create uncertainty for affected parties. He said enforcement agencies must be given sufficient time to conduct thorough investigations, but there should also be a mechanism to ensure complainants are informed of the progress and outcome of their reports within a reasonable period. Jeyenderan said this was particularly important in cases involving businesses and matters with potential implications for government revenue, regulatory compliance and the country’s maritime industry.

items.title: Fire at Bidor FRIM forest, operation resumes this morning
items.summary: IPOH: About 2.42ha of forest area at the Forest Research Institute of Malaysia (FRIM) in Bidor caught fire in an incident yesterday evening. Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said his department received a call about the fire at 5.42pm before a team of personnel from the Bidor Fire and Rescue Station was rushed to the location. He said the operation was suspended at midnight due to safety factors and the condition of the fire that would not spread.

items.title: Decomposed body of unidentified man found in overgrown area in Bukit Jelutong
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 8 — Police have confirmed the discovery of the decomposed body of a man in an overgrown area near Jalan Persiaran Balairong U8, Bukit Jelutong, here yesterday. Shah Alam district police chief ACP Sarudin Samah said police received a public report at about 2.45 pm and sent a team to the scene to investigate. He said police were unable to identify the deceased as no identification documents were found at the scene.

items.title: Six hikers safely rescued after going missing during Trans Gerah expedition in Gunung Gerah
items.summary: GERIK, Sept 8 — Six individuals who were found safe after participating in the Trans Gerah expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, were safely brought out by the search and rescue (SAR) team last night. The Gerik district police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said the rescue team brought all the hikers out of the Kem Kulim and arrived at Kampung Lelar at around 8.45 pm. He said all the victims had previously gathered at Kem Kulim with the rescue team before continuing their journey to Pos Kemar.

items.title: Police open probe into Abdul Hadi’s claim US offered to help topple BN govt in 2014
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have opened an investigation paper into PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s claim that he was once offered cooperation by the United States (US) to topple the Barisan Nasional (BN) government in 2014. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the case is being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code for offences related to statements conducive to public mischief. Abdul Hadi’s statement will also be taken in the near future to complete the investigation,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Ringgit opens almost flat vs greenback amid ongoing west Asia conflict
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit was almost flat against the US dollar at Tuesday's open, as investors remained cautious amid the ongoing West Asia conflict, which continued to drive crude oil prices higher and support the greenback. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the continued conflict suggests US inflation may remain above the US Federal Reserve's two per cent target for a prolonged period. Hence, the US dollar-ringgit could range between RM4.04 and RM4.05 today," he said.

items.title: Trump threatens to block Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier's US sales unless it builds locally
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump threatened Monday to block US sales of Canadian plane maker Bombardier unless it builds aircrafts in the country, complaining of "unjust and unfair" bilateral trade provisions as he escalates a tariff war. And it comes on the eve of Canada imposing retaliatory tariffs on a range of US goods beginning Tuesday. The US market accounts for more than half of Bombardier's revenue, Trump said.

items.title: Nepal disaster: Malaysian families seek answers over search areas, DNA samples
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians who remain uncontactable following landslides and floods at the Nepal-Tibet border want the government to clarify the 'last known locations' being used to guide search efforts by the SMART team. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said families were seeking an immediate and detailed explanation on whether the government had obtained new information on the last known locations of the missing Malaysians. "Does the government now have information or coordinates on the last known locations of Malaysians that differ from those provided by their families?"

items.title: Human rights activist Beverly Joeman dies at 56
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Human rights advocate and former Bersih Sabah vice-chairperson Edlyn Beverly Joeman died today. Beverly died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu after battling acute myeloid leukaemia. She served as Bersih Sabah vice-chairperson from 2016 to 2023.

items.title: Zetrix continues to pursue MYEG Philippines, this time through IPVG
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The saga for the acquisition of MyEG Ventures Inc continues with Zetrix AI Bhd announcing a new deal to acquire a 50 per cent stake in MyEG Ventures Inc for RM130 million from IPVG Employees Inc. Within three days, Zetrix AI announced the deal with Next Lion, terminated it and announced a new deal with IPVG Employees. MyEG Ventures holds a 51 per cent stake in MyEG Philippines.

items.title: Flight data recorders recovered from Amazon cargo plane crash
items.summary: MIAMI: Officials have recovered the flight data recorders from an Amazon cargo plane that overran the runway in Miami and slammed into two vehicles, killing five people, authorities said Monday. One of the vehicles struck in Sunday's accident was a cleaning-services van carrying seven people on airport property, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) chief Jennifer Homendy said. While Homendy refused to discuss the health status of the plane's two pilots, she said the victims were limited to the people in the two vehicles that were struck.

items.title: 2.7 billion exposed to second-hand smoke as deaths hit 1.6 million: Study
items.summary: PARIS: More than 2.7 billion people including children have been exposed to second-hand smoke globally, contributing to nearly 1.7 million deaths in 2023, according to study published Tuesday in The Lancet. Tobacco remains a leading cause of disease globally, the study said, noting many "non-smokers exposed to second-hand smoke" were among the estimate total of 8 million people who died in 2023 of smoking-related illnesses. Among the approximately 2.7 billion people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023 were 767 million children aged 0 to 14, the study found.

items.title: Nepal rescuers focus on 121 hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers searched on Monday for more than 100 hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels days after four miracle rescues from the wreckage of catastrophic floods that laid waste to towns and villages on the Himalayan border with China. The rescues have offered a glimmer of hope as Nepal marked the 13th day after the disaster, traditionally the final day of mourning in Hindu rites, for the hundreds killed in the floods. About 121 of a total 900 people missing from the hydroelectric projects could have been trapped in these tunnels, army rescuers said.

items.title: BN holds advantage as Melaka election arithmetic shifts
items.summary: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia's Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said BN remained well placed to retain the state even without an alliance, but cooperation with PH could maximise its gains. He said PH's strength in urban and non-Malay-majority areas complemented BN's support in rural and Malay-majority constituencies. Universiti Teknologi Mara political analyst Dr Ariff Aizuddin Azlan said BN's established support base meant it could retain the state on its own.

items.title: Nepal mourns as families pray missing loved ones are still alive
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepal held a national day of mourning with candlelight vigils on Monday for victims of devastating glacial floods, as families of missing hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels prayed rescuers might yet find them alive. The Aug 26 glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,399 people, with more than 5,500 missing, including around 800 foreigners. Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet said rescue efforts were continuing at "the same tempo" to make sure "that no one is still stranded."

items.title: Melaka election looms as parties ramp up poll preparations [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Political parties are already putting their election machinery through its paces as Melaka edges towards a possible state election, with Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh hinting that the assembly could be dissolved by the end of the month. Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said the party was preparing to defend its four existing seats while seeking further gains, with discussions on candidates and election machinery already under way. The discussions have already been taking place," he said.

items.title: Nepal floods: What we know so far about unaccounted Malaysians and Malaysia’s relief efforts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Nearly two weeks after devastating floods struck parts of Nepal and the Nepal-Tibet border, rescue and recovery efforts are continuing, with Malaysians among those still unaccounted for. Among those reported uncontactable were Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa and eight other members of his expedition team, including Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) deputy director of the Fire and Rescue Operations Division Mohd Sani Harul. Malaysian relief On September 5, the National Disaster Management Agency deployed an 11-member Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to Nepal to assist in ongoing rescue and disaster relief operations.

items.title: Indonesia names Toba Pulp Lestari suspect in alleged US$113mil tax fraud case
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's Attorney General's Office (AGO) named listed pulp producer Toba Pulp Lestari as a suspect in a case involving alleged tax fraud which resulted in a state loss of around 2 trillion rupiah (US$113 million). The AGO last month named two tax officers as suspects for allegedly accepting bribes from Toba Pulp Lestari. Toba Pulp Lestari did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

items.title: MCMC to meet e-commerce platform operator over drug sale
items.summary: THE Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will meet an e-commerce platform operator over the alleged online sale of drugs. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had expressed concern over the new sale tactics. Also present were Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, his deputy Datuk Rubiah Wang and MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.

items.title: Jakarta airport, four others reopen after Anak Krakatau ash crisis
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's main airport and several other air travel hubs reopened early Tuesday after days of closure due to ash from a volcanic eruption, the Transport Ministry said. Early Tuesday the ministry posted on Instagram that Jakarta's airport and four others are up and running again. Jakarta's main airport wrote on Instagram that "following the current volcanic eruption activity of Mount Anak Krakatau, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has resumed flight operations."

items.title: Zambry: No Malaysians will be denied place at universities
items.summary: THE government commitment to expanding access to higher education means ensuring no Malaysian is denied a place at university because of their background, said Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir yesterday. Zambry said he did not want to see cases where bright students from poor families were unable to pursue tertiary education due to financial hardship. Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris took in four recipients for courses in Chinese language education, Malay language education and special education.

items.title: Singapore ministers face salary debate
items.summary: Singapore pays its political leaders the highest salaries in the world, with a junior minister earning S$1.1 million annually and the prime minister earning S$2.2 million. High ministerial salaries remain a sensitive issue, with median monthly income at S$5,775 last year. By comparison, the British prime minister earns US$230,000, while United States President Donald Trump earns US$400,000.

items.title: Bangladesh dengue outbreak accelerates, straining hospitals
items.summary: BANGLADESH'S dengue outbreak is accelerating, with 42,590 people hospitalised and 117 deaths recorded this year, as a sharp surge strains hospitals and raises fears the disease could intensify further in the coming weeks. At least four dengue patients died and 1,558 others were hospitalised in the past 24 hours, according to health ministry data, marking the highest daily admission tally recorded so far this year. Health experts also warn that September could prove even more severe than August, which recorded the highest monthly dengue caseload of the year.

items.title: Over 3,000 celebrate Malaysia's colours, flavours & heritage at Malaysia Carnival in UK
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A vibrant celebration of Malaysia's colours, flavours, heritage, and community spirit at the Malaysia Carnival 2026 drew more than 3,000 people from across the United Kingdom to the Tun Abdul Razak Research Centre in Hertfordshire on Saturday. Malaysian High Commissioner-Designate to the United Kingdom, Datuk Dr Azfar Mohamad Mustafar, officiated the event organised by the High Commission of Malaysia in London, delivering a message that celebrated the shared spirit, diversity, and heritage connecting Malaysians and friends of Malaysia. The carnival also showcased Malaysia's rich performing arts, beginning with traditional percussion and folk arts such as kompang and dikir barat, followed by traditional Malaysian songs and a powerful Silat Seni Gayong demonstration that highlighted the nation's living martial arts heritage.

items.title: Thai DPM Sihasak leaves Malaysia after Two-day working visit
items.summary: SEPANG: Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sihasak Phuangketkeow departed for home after concluding his two-day working visit to Malaysia. In 2025, Thailand was the sixth largest trading partner globally and the second largest among ASEAN Member States, with total trade amounting to RM118.57 billion (US$27.73 billion). From January to July 2026, bilateral trade between the two countries reached RM85.01 billion (US$21.13 billion), compared with RM66.95 billion (US$16.64 billion) during the corresponding period in 2025, reflecting the continued strong growth and potential of economic ties between the two countries.

items.title: King Charles confirms Harry and Meghan remain non-working royals
items.summary: LONDON: King Charles authorised a letter to senior British officials on Monday confirming that his youngest son Harry and Harry's wife Meghan remain non-working royals following their return to the UK. The letter, which was shared with Harry's team and sent as guidance to senior officials in the government and military, said that after Harry and Meghan stepped down from official royal duties in 2020 they "are no longer working Members of The Royal Family." Prince Harry and his family arrived back in Britain late last month, six years after quitting royal duties and moving to the United States.

items.title: NST Leader: Plugging cracks in cross-border drug trade through shared intelligence
items.summary: AS enforcement by Malaysia and Indonesia gets more robust, drug syndicates operate across borders and employ more complex methods to evade detection by authorities. In July, a Malaysia Airlines pilot managed to slip past detectors with 26kg of ecstasy pills hidden in his luggage. He also tested positive for cocaine, ecstasy pills and methamphetamine.

items.title: Robots protest rampant AI in Poland
items.summary: WARSAW: Waving flags, "chanting" slogans, and marching in circles: around 30 robots took to the streets of Warsaw on Monday to campaign for AI regulation in front of the Polish digital affairs ministry. "The robots present here are meant to show that this technology is already a reality," Agibot A3, one of the AI-powered humanoid robots, told AFP. "These robots can already move around freely, they're already 'protesting'", he said.

items.title: Anwar congratulates TMJ, hails his sporting excellence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Tunku Ismail, Regent of Johor, after he was named Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament (JSCPT) 2026. "Congratulations to His Royal Highness Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Regent of Johor, on being named the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament 2026, while also leading Royal Johor to lift this prestigious title," he said. Tunku Ismail was named MVP yesterday after delivering an outstanding performance throughout the tournament.

items.title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's main airport postponed reopening on Monday after halting operations following a volcanic eruption that left hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded. Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150km from Indonesia's capital, Jakarta, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and a plume of volcanic ash. Airports closed Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport extended its closure from Monday morning to midnight.

items.title: Secret Assad-era Syrian nuclear reactor was almost complete
items.summary: VIENNA: A near-complete nuclear reactor built secretly during the rule of toppled Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad would have been able to produce material to make nuclear weapons, the UN nuclear watchdog chief said on Monday. Inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) last month visited two sites, one in Deir Ezzor and a second undisclosed location identified to them by Syrian authorities. In a report seen by AFP last week, the IAEA said Syria's previous government was building a nuclear reactor.

items.title: Man found dead at house in Kota Belud
items.summary: KOTA BELUD: A 23-year-old man was found dead at a house here today. Kota Belud police chief Superintendent Khairul Shah Peri said police received a report on the incident at 4.20pm. Khairul Shah said police were continuing investigations to determine the cause of death.

items.title: MAHB: 41 flights to Jakarta cancelled following Anak Krakatau eruption
items.summary: The airport operator said that Penang International Airport recorded seven cancellations, followed by Subang Airport with two, while Kuching International Airport and Kota Kinabalu International Airport recorded one cancellation each. No cancellations were recorded at Kota Bharu Airport. The cancellations followed the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after volcanic ash from the Anak Krakatau eruption affected flight operations.

items.title: Four-month old baby dies after found unconscious at Dungun childcare centre
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 7 — A four-month-old baby girl died after being found unconscious at a childcare centre in Bandar Al Muktafi Billah Shah (AMBS) near here today. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the incident at 3.41 pm. Nik Ab Halim said medical personnel at the hospital conducted examinations and resuscitation efforts, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but the baby was pronounced dead at about 12.45 pm.

items.title: Police: Six missing Gunung Trans Gerah hikers contacted, safe for now
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 7 — Six individuals, including two children, who were reported missing while trekking along the Gunung Trans Gerah trail in Lojing, Gua Musang, have managed to make contact this afternoon and reported that they are safe. Gerik police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said information regarding the group’s condition was received at about 5.30 pm today after a family member managed to contact one of the mountain guides accompanying the group. Abdul Samad said the method for extracting the group - whether by land or air - will be determined based on their condition and location after the SAR team manages to meet the victims.

items.title: Malaysians urged to register on Foreign Ministry’s E-Konsular as precaution, though not mandatory
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Recent developments around the world, arising from natural disasters and geopolitical situations, have increased the need for Malaysians to register with the Foreign Affairs Ministry’s e-Konsular system to provide information on their whereabouts. For instance, when major floods occurred in Nepal last month, information on Malaysians there was obtained only from their relatives back home and travel agencies used by Malaysians travelling to the country. According to the ekonsular.kln.gov.my website, the registration is intended to systematically record the whereabouts of Malaysians overseas.

items.title: Malaysia deploying DNA experts to identify disaster victims, pending Nepal’s go-ahead
items.summary: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia had submitted a request to deploy the experts, with the DNA identification process expected to begin after search and rescue (SAR) operations conclude. He said the expertise was needed to match DNA samples taken from recovered bodies with samples provided by the families of Malaysian citizens who remain missing. “We need DNA to match against the DNA samples from the families of the Malaysian citizens.

items.title: Elderly man remanded four days for slashing wife’s hand
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 7 — An elderly man suspected of slashing his wife’s right hand with a machete at Taman Desa Sejahtera here today has been remanded for four days from yesterday to assist in investigations. Kota Tinggi Police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the incident at about 9.30 pm was believed to have followed an argument over the television volume, which the victim, also in her 70s, allegedly had turned up too high. He said the victim sustained a small wound, about one centimetre long, to her right hand and was treated at Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: Police tracking down 10 suspects to assist in murder, gang fight in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — Police are tracking down 10 men to assist in the investigation of two separate fight cases in Taman Alam Megah and Taman Sri Muda here last month. Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said of that number, seven men are wanted to assist in the investigation of a fight in Taman Alam Megah that resulted in the death of a 23-year-old local man on Aug 25. He said following both cases, police conducted a series of raids in Shah Alam, as well as Lenga and Iskandar Puteri, Johor, between Aug 14 and 28.

items.title: Housing Ministry: Check Teduh to check project, developer information before buying property
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The public, particularly prospective homebuyers, are encouraged to check information on developers and housing projects through the TEDUH portal and mobile application before making a purchase decision to reduce the risk of encountering problems later. The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said TEDUH, developed by the National Housing Department (JPN), is a one-stop platform providing access to information such as developers’ licence status, advertising permit and developer’s licence (APDL), project progress and information related to private housing projects. The public can access the TEDUH Portal via teduh.kpkt.gov.my or use the TEDUH mobile application.

items.title: Over 26,000 new undergraduates to benefit from RM1,500 PTPTN advance payments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) continues to strengthen the nation’s higher education empowerment agenda by offering Loan Advance Payments (WPP) totaling RM1,500 to eligible new students to help cover part of the initial preparation costs for admission to public universities and polytechnics. In a statement, PTPTN said the RM39.7 million scheme benefits 26,457 students entering bachelor’s degree programmes at public universities and polytechnics for the September 2026 intake. “The WPP is available to Malaysian citizens who opted into the scheme when applying to public higher education institutions via UPUOnline or university websites.

items.title: Malaysia rail link: ECRL passenger fares to be known by year-end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Passenger fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) have not been finalised and an official announcement will be made by the end of this year, said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL). MRL said in a statement on the ECRL Facebook page today that a recently recirculated information on social media regarding the passenger fares is inaccurate and has never been verified by any authority. The company said the official passenger fares for the ECRL will only be announced by the Ministry of Transport Malaysia once the relevant evaluation and approval processes are finalised.

items.title: Minden air quality hits unhealthy level as API rises to 142, says Penang exco
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — Air quality in parts of Penang island reached an unhealthy level today, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading climbing to 142 at 3pm. Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu said the Minden air-quality monitoring station on the island began recording unhealthy readings at 9am. Sundarajoo said Penang’s air quality had generally remained at good to moderate levels between September 4 and 6.

items.title: No cracks in federal unity govt, says Pakatan minister as Umno closes gap with PAS ahead of assembly
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — PKR today denied speculations of turmoil among federal unity government components following developments in Umno’s ties with PAS. PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Pakatan Harapan (PH) continues to maintain good relations with BN, despite Umno’s strategic cooperation with PAS. “So far, there are no issues, and all Umno ministers still attended last week's Cabinet meeting.

items.title: Selangor police say investigation into Sunway Lagoon ride gone wrong to take at least three months as it waits for tech report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The investigation into the August 22 roller coaster incident at Sunway Lagoon that injured 10 visitors could take another three to four months. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said this is because investigators are waiting for technical reports from several agencies before they can wrap up the case. He said police were working with the occupational safety and health department (DOSH), Fire and Rescue Department, forensic teams and other agencies on the investigation.

items.title: No seat for Pakatan at annual Umno assembly, but PAS gets red carpet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Umno will not be inviting its federal government partner Pakatan Harapan (PH) to its general assembly, starting this Wednesday to Saturday. Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PAS was invited instead, as a reciprocal gesture for the invitation to the Islamist party’s 72nd congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, last weekend. “Society wants Malays to champion Malay unity — not just within Umno, but across Malay parties.

items.title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer
items.summary: Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur. “In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.

items.title: Two Fridays to go? Melaka CM Ab Rauf drops biggest hint yet on state assembly dissolution
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 7 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month, paving the way for a state election. The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said the dissolution would come in “two more Fridays”, suggesting an announcement could be made within the next two weeks, Harian Metro reported. His remarks came a day after Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged Ab Rauf to speed up the dissolution announcement to allow the people, particularly young voters, to decide the state’s future.
